unresolved_intent.rationale: Spec requires blocking pipelines where any later stage writes. Full analysis requires parsing each command in the pipeline, which introduces shell-syntax complexity and potential for bypass. Conservative approach: all pipes block when .approved is referenced, fail-closed.

Guard maintains a curated set of tools provably read-only (Read, Grep, Glob, browser read tools, etc.). Hundreds of MCP and browser tools exist; not all are included because tool-by-tool inspection is expensive and unknown tools correctly default-deny per AC-GH-06.

is_read_only_command() checks hardcoded keywords and patterns (rm, mv, cp, sed, git, output redirection). Many other write operations exist (dd, tee, install, truncate, etc.). Completeness trades off against false negatives; conservative fail-closed approach flags doubt.

Spec explicitly states symlinks, scripts with indirect effects, runtime-assembled filenames, and child processes are out of reach by design. Guard inspects text/structure only; measured byte-level control lives elsewhere.
